paragraphs: Here's the hard part, friend. God tells Jerusalem she sank so low that her sisters, Sodom and Samaria, "appear righteous" next to her (Ezekiel 16:51). The text says Sodom was "arrogant, overfed, and complacent" and "did not help the poor and needy" (Ezekiel 16:49). Pride and comfort can creep in without any alarm going off, and the passage warns us to watch for them. Looking at somebody else's mess never makes our own cleaner, and Jerusalem found that out the hard way.

Then comes the turn, and I want you to hold onto it. God says, "But I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you" (Ezekiel 16:60). Jerusalem broke the oath, and God still says He will remember. The passage says He will restore Sodom, Samaria and Jerusalem too (Ezekiel 16:53). I know what it feels like to think you're done for, and this is a God who doesn't throw people away.

And look at how it ends. God says, "I will make atonement for all you have done" (Ezekiel 16:63). She doesn't earn her way back. He does the work, and she comes to know that He is the LORD (Ezekiel 16:62). So if you've got a pile of regret, friend, don't hide it and don't pretend. Bring it to the One who makes atonement, and let Him do what only He can do.
